sources.articleTitle: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
Solange Alexandre, WWII French resistant, dies at 104

headline: French Resistance Fighter Solange Alexandre Passes Away At Age 104
metaDescription: Solange Alexandre, a notable French Resistance member who served as a spy and leader during World War II, has passed away at the age of 104.
aiSummaryBullets: Solange Alexandre, a French Resistance operative during World War II, has died at the age of 104.
Known by the code name Corlay, she acted as a liaison agent and spy for the French Forces of the Interior.
She led a resistance group named Pas-de-Bœuf, managed sabotage operations, and protected Allied personnel.
aiContextParagraph: Solange Alexandre was a significant figure within the French Resistance during the German occupation of France in the Second World War. Operating under the pseudonym Corlay, she performed intelligence and liaison work before establishing the Pas-de-Bœuf resistance unit in 1944. Reports indicate that she held the rank of lieutenant within the French Forces of the Interior by the end of the conflict. Her wartime contributions included orchestrating various sabotage missions against occupying forces and providing safe shelter for Allied airmen. Beyond her administrative and strategic roles, she was noted for her command over a group of 30 fighters. Her passing marks the loss of a recognized veteran who played an active part in the European theater of World War II.
whyItIsViral: The story gained traction across multiple international news outlets, reflecting high interest in the legacy of World War II veterans.
